clue.text: Prayer of a bird held in its bill

indicators.note: the bird and the A are held inside the bill, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a bill is a printed notice stuck on a wall, a poster
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A churchgoer's devotions somehow involve a bird clutched in its own beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a beak beside 'bird', but it is the posted notice; A TERN goes in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin opening words 'Our Father' give the name to the Lord's Prayer said in Latin.

clue.text: Biblical character who makes a joke

parts.note: a gag is a comedian's joke

explanation.surface: A figure from scripture turns out to be a comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Agag is the Amalekite king spared by Saul and killed by Samuel in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Cheese which, is the reverse of manufactured

indicators.note: the clue says to take the word for manufactured and read it backwards

parts.note: manufactured goods are made

explanation.surface: A cheese described as the opposite of a factory product.
explanation.definitionFit: A round Dutch cheese with a red wax rind, named after a town in Holland.

clue.text: Almost going north too soon

parts.note: arriving too soon is being early

explanation.surface: Someone nearly sets off northwards before time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean all but, very close to completely.

clue.text: Team whose hut holds a group of fighting men in an iron grip

indicators.note: the hut holds the other letters, so they go inside it

parts.note: a shed is a hut

indicators.note: the iron grips the fighting men, so their letters sit between the two letters for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a field unit is a body of soldiers in the field

explanation.surface: A team's clubhouse holds soldiers in a vice-like hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'grip' signals the inner one, where the iron grips the soldiers, and 'holds' the outer one, with the hut wrapped round everything. 'Iron grip' reads as a phrase, but it is two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield United is an English professional football club, nicknamed the Blades.

clue.text: Select groups are back in the part of Somerset I left

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Upper classes are returning to a district of Somerset that the speaker left.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Somerset I left' backwards to find the run inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The chosen few, the cream of a group, are its select members.

clue.text: Trains begin turning into ships

indicators.note: turning tells us the letters of the two words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Locomotives start to turn into sailing vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-masted sailing vessels, square-rigged on the foremast, once used by pirates.

clue.text: Make underground place in Sussex ask questions

parts.note: to inter is to bury, putting a body below ground
Rogate is a village in West Sussex, a county on England's south coast

explanation.surface: Building a subterranean spot in a southern county.
explanation.definitionFit: To question someone closely and formally, as police do a suspect.

clue.text: Nothing was in a hurry in Africa

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
someone who ran was hurrying

explanation.surface: Somebody who had nothing to do rushed about on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a place found in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Oran is a port city on the coast of Algeria, in North Africa.

clue.text: America is corrupt and good fellowship is surprisingly dear in it

indicators.note: in says the second jumble goes inside the first
corrupt means spoilt or distorted, so these letters are jumbled
surprisingly hints that the next word appears in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A claim that America is rotten, yet comradeship is unexpectedly cherished there.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate jumbles: 'corrupt' scrambles the country into CAMARIE and 'surprisingly' scrambles the endearment into ADER, which goes inside the first after its fifth letter; 'it' points back to the jumbled country.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual trust and friendship among comrades is fellowship.

clue.text: Glance this way, being seen in the fog less clearly

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the words that follow, spanning them

explanation.surface: Someone peers through thinning fog.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at someone with obvious amorous interest is to cast eyes their way.

clue.text: Unselfish when opponents are in front of one inside the box

indicators.note: inside puts one piece within the box

parts.note: a crate is a wooden box

parts.words: when opponents are in front of one
parts.note: in football a player is not offside when enough opponents are ahead of them, so is onside

explanation.surface: A selfless player waits while rivals stand before them in the penalty area.
explanation.walkthrough: Football's offside law: a player is not offside when at least two opponents are level with or ahead of them, so the long phrase defines that state. 'Box' tempts as the penalty area but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughtful of others' needs, so not selfish.

clue.text: A soldier is correct about nothing 'if he lets a deserter go

indicators.note: lets here means lets in, admitting a piece inside
about means the word for correct goes around the nought

parts.note: proper means correct
O, zero, means nothing
a rat is one who deserts a cause, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A soldier is right to have no qualms about letting a turncoat escape.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside PROPER to make PROOPER; then A RAT is let in after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratrooper is an airborne soldier who drops by parachute.

clue.text: Bungled, being down on a journalist

parts.note: down is fine soft fluff
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone botched an interview by being harsh on a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down on' looks like criticising, but down is soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluffing a line or catch means making a mess of it.

clue.text: Girl who panics?

definitions.meaning: a fashionable young woman of the 1920s

explanation.definitionFit: A 1920s young woman of bold fashion; also, playfully, one who gets into a flap.

clue.text: Decline to get rid of the smell?

definitions.meaning: a going down or downward slope

definitions.text: to get rid of the smell?
definitions.meaning: read whimsically as ..., removing a scent

explanation.definitionFit: A going down is a decline; split as de-scent it removes an odour.

clue.text: Making nothing revive with the mouth

parts.note: O, zero, means nothing
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: A patient who was nearly dead is brought round by mouth-to-mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Done by speech or taken by mouth, as medicine taken by mouth.

clue.text: French river right for the fisherman

parts.note: the Seine flows through Paris

explanation.surface: A Parisian river suits the angler.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fishes with a seine, a large vertical net.

clue.text: Congregate in making an impression as a hobby

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: stamping is pressing a mark into something
to collect is to gather together

explanation.surface: Gathering together to impress people as a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Philately, gathering postage stamps, is a classic pastime.

clue.text: Turn gloomy when a box appears in the study

indicators.note: the box appears inside the study, one piece within another

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A room grows dim when a crate turns up in the study.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow dark or dim is to become gloomy.

clue.text: Most up-to date, like us in the home

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a cosy one
we is the subject form of us

explanation.surface: The latest thing, like us at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent, the latest, is the most up to date.

clue.text: Still about five turn up

indicators.note: about tells us the word for still goes around the numeral

parts.note: inert means motionless, still
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Five people standing motionless about to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like arrive, but it means turn upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To invert is to turn upside down.

clue.text: Confine one after the other by the sound of it

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is a word pronounced like the phrase before

parts.note: in turn means one after another

explanation.surface: Prisoners are locked up one by one, so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to detain or imprison, especially in wartime.

clue.text: On the throne so expecting to lose one's head'?

indicators.note: losing one's head means removing the first letter of the word

parts.note: an expectant mother is pregnant

explanation.surface: A queen who is with child fears execution.
explanation.walkthrough: Regnant follows a title, as in Queen Regnant, a reigning monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant means reigning, so a ruling sovereign is enthroned.

clue.text: Bird makes love in the country

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the country

parts.note: ROK is the abbreviation for Republic of Korea
love is nil in tennis scoring, shown as O

explanation.surface: A bird makes love in a rural area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like the countryside but is South Korea as ROK.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is a black bird of the crow family.

definitions.text: who puts one in the shade?
